applied.quote: At ModernWallet, we write plain-language guides on where to keep cash, and the money market account vs money market fund question starts with the name: the same two words label a bank product and an investment product.
applied.replacement: At The Modern Wallet, we write plain-language money guides, and the money market account vs money market fund question starts with the name: the same two words label a bank product and an investment product.
applied.why: Self-description names The Modern Wallet and plain-language money guides, not cash-placement guides

applied.quote: Anything sold as shares, priced at net asset value, or described in a prospectus or shareholder report is a mutual fund.
applied.replacement: Mutual fund shares are priced at net asset value, and a money market fund has a prospectus and shareholder report.
applied.why: SOURCE describes mutual fund shares and NAV; not that all such products are funds

applied.quote: If you already hold cash at a brokerage, a money market fund bought there skips the step of moving money to a bank, with the trade-off of no FDIC coverage.
applied.replacement: If you already hold cash at a brokerage, a money market fund bought there comes with the trade-off of no FDIC coverage.
applied.why: SOURCE does not state a brokerage fund avoids moving money to a bank

applied.quote: The main limits of a money market account are a variable rate and FDIC coverage that stops at $250,000 per depositor, per FDIC-insured bank, per ownership category.
applied.replacement: Limits of a money market account include a variable rate and FDIC coverage that stops at $250,000 per depositor, per FDIC-insured bank, per ownership category.
applied.why: SOURCE does not rank any limit as main
